verdict.rationale: The only evidence close to this story is Bridge's orchestration layer, which programmatically supports ramp flows and offers static templates that give customers persistent, reusable deposit instructions. This roughly approximates per-customer deposit provisioning, but nothing documents API-created wallets. Stripe's stablecoin financial accounts and connected-account USDC balances are business-held balances or dashboard wallet linking, not programmatically provisioned wallets. Missing for 10: documented API to create per-customer or per-purpose wallets, explicit on-chain deposit address provisioning, key custody semantics (custodial vs. non-custodial, key management), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can create wallets programmatically — per-customer or per-purpose wallets and deposit addresses provisioned through the API with documented key custody semantics

citations.quote: A static template provides persistent deposit instructions your customers can use repeatedly.
Programmatically support on-ramps, off-ramps, and crypto-to-crypto flows.
